assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: clinical trial
items.clue: The stage of drug development that uses healthy volunteers and patients.

items.label: antibiotic
items.clue: A medicine, such as penicillin, that helps to cure bacterial disease by killing infective bacteria inside the body.

items.label: preclinical testing
items.clue: The stage of drug development done in a laboratory using cells, tissues and live animals, before the drug is given to people.

items.label: vaccination
items.clue: Introducing small quantities of dead or inactive forms of a pathogen into the body to stimulate the white blood cells to produce antibodies.

questions.stem: What is introduced into the body during a vaccination?

options.text: Dead or inactive forms of a pathogen
Ready-made antibodies from donors
Live and active forms of a pathogen
An antibiotic that kills pathogens

questions.explanation: Vaccination involves introducing small quantities of dead or inactive forms of a pathogen into the body to stimulate the white blood cells to produce antibodies.

questions.stem: A patient has a viral infection and a painful sore throat. Which treatment is appropriate, and why?

options.text: Antibiotics, which kill the pathogen
Painkillers, which destroy the virus
Painkillers, which treat the symptoms
Antitoxins, which kill the pathogen

questions.explanation: Painkillers and other medicines are used to treat the symptoms of disease but do not kill pathogens, so they are the appropriate treatment for the pain of a viral infection.

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical company has synthesised a possible new drug. Which describes the preclinical testing of that drug?

options.text: Testing on healthy volunteers, patients
Testing on cells, tissues and live animals
Testing on patients at the optimum dose
Testing on some patients given a placebo

questions.explanation: Preclinical testing is done in a laboratory using cells, tissues and live animals, before the drug is given to any person.

questions.stem: A large proportion of the population in a town is vaccinated against measles. What is the effect on the people in that town who are not vaccinated?

options.text: They are equally likely to catch measles
They are made immune to measles as well
They are less likely to catch measles
They must be given antibiotics instead

questions.explanation: The spread of pathogens can be reduced by immunising a large proportion of the population, so an unvaccinated person is less likely to meet the measles virus.

questions.stem: The use of antibiotics greatly reduced deaths from infectious bacterial diseases, but some bacterial infections are now much harder to treat. Why?

options.text: Patients have grown resistant to antibiotics
Antibiotics have started to kill viruses too
Bacteria now reproduce inside human cells
Resistant strains of bacteria have emerged

questions.explanation: The emergence of strains resistant to antibiotics is of great concern, because those strains are not killed by the antibiotic that once cured the disease.

questions.stem: What happens in a double blind trial?

options.text: Some patients get a smaller dose
Healthy volunteers are in the trial
Some patients are given a placebo
Each patient gets the optimum dose

questions.explanation: In double blind trials, some patients are given a placebo rather than the drug being tested.

questions.stem: Why is it difficult to develop drugs that kill viruses?

options.text: Viruses live in cells, so tissues are damaged
Viruses reproduce outside the body's cells
Viruses make toxins that destroy the drugs
Viruses are easily destroyed by antibiotics

questions.explanation: Viruses live and reproduce inside cells, so it is difficult to develop drugs that kill viruses without also damaging the body's tissues.

questions.stem: Which drug is correctly matched with the source it originally came from?

options.text: Aspirin is extracted from foxgloves
Penicillin is extracted from foxgloves
Digitalis is extracted from foxgloves
Digitalis is extracted from the willow

questions.explanation: Traditionally drugs were extracted from plants and microorganisms, and the heart drug digitalis originates from foxgloves.

questions.stem: Why must new medical drugs be tested and trialled before they are used?

options.text: To check they are safe and effective
To check they kill bacterial pathogens
To check they remove painful symptoms
To check patients cannot resist drugs

questions.explanation: New medical drugs have to be tested and trialled before being used to check that they are safe and effective, which is why they are extensively tested for toxicity, efficacy and dose.

questions.stem: How are most new drugs produced today?

options.text: Extracted from plants and microorganisms
Extracted from the willow and foxgloves
Collected from moulds growing in soil
Synthesised by pharmaceutical chemists

questions.explanation: Most new drugs are synthesised by chemists in the pharmaceutical industry, although the starting point may still be a chemical extracted from a plant.
